sources.title: The Destruction and Dispossession of Rohingya Land and Property during the 2017 Clearance Operations: Public Summary
sources.by: United Nations Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar

sources.title: Report of the detailed findings of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar (A/HRC/39/CRP.2)

entries.text: The report says none of the Rohingya villages of U Daung village tract survived the operations that began on 25 August 2017. What was left was demolished: photographs from April 2018 show bulldozed land, and the marketplace was bulldozed by late 2018. The No. 4 Border Guard Police battalion base, begun in 2016, was extended over the former marketplace.

The report says Rohingya homes, markets and religious buildings in Myo Thu Gyi village tract were burned and razed in the operations that began on 25 August 2017. By early 2018 a company had cleared over 411 acres of burned Rohingya land here with heavy machinery.
Satellite imagery showed 307 intact structures in Kan Kya (North) before the violence.
Satellite imagery showed 518 intact structures in Kan Kya (South) before the violence. By 2019 the No. 5 Border Guard Police battalion base had been built directly over the former village.

The report says fires were detected in Inn Din on 28 August 2017, and that by 22 September 2017 nearly all of Inn Din (East, Middle, Rakhine and West) had been destroyed: 719 of 739 structures. The No. 6 Border Guard Police battalion base, about 75 hectares, was built from late 2017 and largely finished by August 2019.
The report says the base was built directly over the remains of Inn Din (East) and Inn Din (Rakhine).

The report says Bo Bar, Done Paik and Ree Dar were fully destroyed between 25 August and mid-October 2017, first by fire; the few buildings left were demolished between October 2017 and April 2018. Before, there were about 400 structures in Bo Bar, 431 in Done Paik and 364 in Ree Dar.
The No. 7 Border Guard Police battalion base was built on the land where Done Paik and Ree Dar stood. Building began in early 2018 and went on until 21 April 2021.

The report says Rohingya farmland in Ah Lel Chaung village tract was seized in early December 2017 for the No. 8 Border Guard Police battalion base. Villagers lost hundreds of acres; the 333-acre base stood on their rice fields by January 2020.

The report says Rohingya homes, shops and schools in Myin Hlut were burned in the August 2017 operations and whole areas were later bulldozed; a company cleared 418 acres of burned Rohingya land. The No. 9 Border Guard Police battalion base, about 85 hectares, stood on the site of demolished Rohingya villages by 2021.

The report says Rohingya land in Zin Paing Nyar village tract was burned around 28 August 2017, and a company then cleared over 432 acres here and in neighbouring tracts. The No. 10 Border Guard Police battalion base was built over villagers’ land in this tract.
Former residents of Hpu Khar Li told the investigators their land was absorbed into the base. Video shows barbed-wire fences and a watchtower along a road in the village.
The Mission’s report describes in detail what its witnesses said happened in this village in late August 2017.
